introduction.text:
This fragment written in an Early Neo-Assyrian hand contains the remains of 36 ll. of one column and the first signs of some 10 ll. of a second column to the right of the first one. No edges are preserved, nor is the reverse of the tablet. As first identified by J.D. Hawkins (@i{apud} @bib{wiseman_gilgamesh_1975@157 fn. 6}), the piece parallels ll. 19-54 and 109-113 + 118-122 of Tablet I of the SB Epic of Gilgameš.

Another piece of evidence for Gilgameš in Kalḫu is the tablet @url{/fragmentarium/IM.67564}{ND.4381} (@i{CTN} 4, 153). This other tablet, however, seems to deviate considerably in wording (and sometimes even in macrostructure) from the SB chapters it partially parallels.

In comparison to ND.4381, the contents of the present fragment fit much more neatly in the reconstructed text of the SB version. Still, the distribution of its lines to columns seems to deviate, from the common practice of writing Gilgameš on triple-column tablets with about 40-50 ll. per column. The difference between the line numbers in cols. i and ii of the present fragment suggests a column length of about 75 ll. per column. Consequently, the original tablet comprised only two columns on each side (unless it held more than one chapter of the Epic). 

As the manuscript discussed here is already included in the @url{/corpus/L/1/4/SB/I}{eBL Literature Corpus} edition, it will not be re-edited here.
